body:
Founder real-time bug report: a Colab training run's very first env.reset() raised 'TimeoutError: no live respawn snapshot within timeout' with zero other diagnostic output anywhere in the log. Investigation: fetched the real, live TRAINING_GROUND level (id=13, the current is_default_queue level) export and ran a local bin/shank_server with the exact same --deathmatch --fast-forward --level flags rl_train_packet.py's own _spawn_server uses -- a real UDP client connected and received a valid alive snapshot within ~1 second, no crash, no hang, ruling out an obvious logic regression in today's own earlier server-side changes (S477/S478/S480) against this specific level's real data (it has zero characters/doors/exits authored, so those code paths were no-ops here anyway). Could not reproduce the actual reported failure locally. Real, found-live, separate gap found and fixed along the way: _spawn_server (the function that launches the real training server subprocess, used by both the main training loop and the eval path) redirected stdout/stderr to subprocess.DEVNULL unconditionally -- the exact same class of bug S459-61 already found and fixed for the two eval bots ('these two bots used to run with stdout/stderr silenced entirely... a real crash... was invisible, indistinguishable in the log from a genuine 0-0 tie'), left unfixed here for the server itself. If the server binary ever crashes or fails to start (stale/broken build, missing shared library, a Colab-specific environment gap), nothing about why was ever visible -- just an opaque downstream TimeoutError 30 seconds later, indistinguishable from a genuinely slow-but-working server. Fixed: stdout/stderr now capture to a real log file (output_dir/server_<port>.log, matching _spawn_frozen_policy_bot's own established log_path convention), and the process is checked for an early exit right after the existing startup grace period -- a dead server is now an immediate, loud RuntimeError naming the log file and printing its own tail. Live-verified both paths directly (happy path: real non-empty log with the expected STARTUP line; failure path: SERVER_BIN pointed at /bin/false raises the new RuntimeError with real exit code + log tail). Existing test_rl_registry.py suite still passes (5/5, unaffected). Commit 4cff907 (fix) + 5ae4ff6 (changelog). Honest, explicitly not fully resolved: this fix makes the NEXT occurrence immediately diagnosable, it does not explain what already happened to the founder -- asked them to re-run and report back what the new log shows if it recurs.

⚓ ☃
title: RL training: surface real server crash/startup failures instead of silent DEVNULL
